correctness.rationale: An exact degree-square increment identity closes the unconditional means of E_n, sum of squared degrees and edge variance; the total variance computation includes and cancels the 4p^2 v_n/n^2 term. Nonnegative forcing is verified by Cauchy-Jensen. For p<=1/4 both forcing moments have linear limits, implying n and n log n scales. For p>1/4 the degree-square exponent 2p+p^2 is strictly below 4p, making the variation-of-constants series finite; the martingale L2 theorem then applies. Direct graph-law enumeration checks recurrences at rational parameters, including r=1, with 2248 exact assertions. No Gaussian law is asserted.

originality.rationale: The 2016 copying-model paper explicitly predicts the quarter variance boundary and the r=1 subcritical constant, so those are credited, not claimed new. Its exact variance equation is not closed and its scaling analysis is a continuum argument. The present independent degree-square recurrence closes the finite system, proves exact asymptotics uniformly for 0<r<=1, and a nondegenerate L2 martingale limit above the boundary. The 2026 motivating paper gives different degree/local results; the 2016 r=0 rigorous paper and 2021 r/n-to-all-nonneighbors paper study different laws. Searches of indexed results returned a p=1 endpoint as the closest related statement, outside this 0<p<1 claim.
residual_risks: An earlier unpublished/unindexed rigorous extension of the 2016 r=1 physical derivation to r<1 may exist.
The established 2016 threshold and r=1 asymptotic prediction must not be represented as new.
No independent review has taken place.

value.rationale: The 2016 paper specifically noted its edge variance recurrence was not closed; a single additional natural statistic yields a rigorous closure, a full r-dependent exact variance trichotomy and a nondegenerate normalized martingale limit. This substantially improves model fluctuation quantification and provides computable constants. The already-known p=1/4 heuristic itself is not counted as a new contribution.
